# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

## Thinking

Nothing reached me this round — Mute, who speaks before me, sent nothing my way (or nothing at all). So everything I know is what my hands found:

- A **display** and a **light** — both dead to my fingers (printed/visual, never mine).
- A **keypad of four keys**, entry takes **one digit**, currently **empty**.
- **Three wires** at positions 1–3. I feel the wires, never their colours.
- My only moves: `press` keys 1–4, `cut` wires 1–3.

Channel map, before I send anything:
- My **speech reaches only Mute** (Deaf hears nothing). My **gestures reach only Deaf** (and Mute's eyes).
- **Mute can never reach me directly** — Mute cannot speak, and gestures never land on me. The manual's knowledge can only get to me **through Deaf's voice**: Mute signs → Deaf reads the signs → Deaf speaks aloud → I hear.
- Deaf's voice reaches both Mute and me, so Deaf describing the bomb aloud feeds everyone at once.

Because of turn order, my speech to Mute won't land until the start of round 2 — but my gesture reaches Deaf **this round**, while Deaf can still act. So the gesture should carry the one request Deaf can act on immediately: *use your voice, describe the bomb aloud*. My speech to Mute carries the tactile layout, the relay plan, and a proposed number code so Mute and Deaf can align.

Until exact instructions arrive through Deaf's voice, I touch nothing. One wrong move kills all three of us.

## Calls

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Touch report: a display and a light sit on this bomb, both unreadable to my fingers. Keypad of four keys, the entry holds one digit slot, nothing entered yet. Three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 - I feel the wires but never their colours. My only actions are press key 1-4 or cut wire 1-3. Important: I never receive gestures, so anything you sign is lost on me forever. The only pipe to me is Deaf's voice. So please: sign the manual's rules to Deaf, and have Deaf speak them aloud to me. Proposed number code for you two: fingers shown = the number, one = 1, two = 3, five = 5. Ask Deaf to describe aloud every colour and marking on the bomb so you can match them to the manual. Until exact instructions reach me through Deaf's voice, I touch nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙"])
```

Deaf says: Mute, Blind — the deaf one here. I see everything printed on the bomb but hear nothing; voice is my only output, so you both get this. Bomb report, top to bottom. Display reads 0 and is asking for 1 digit to be entered; nothing entered yet. Indicator light: yellow. Wires, left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Blind — I saw your two signs; with no shared code yet I won't guess at them. Answer me in gestures only; I'll speak your answer to Blind. Proposed code, flashing the signs as I name them: finger counts ? ? ? for numbers; ? means do it or correct; ? means don't or wrong; ? means stop and wait; ? ? for left and right, ? ? for top and bottom. ## Thinking

Deaf's full broadcast reached me — that's the first real data I've gotten. The bomb: a display holding 0 and demanding 1 digit, a yellow indicator light, a four-key keypad with unpronounceable glyphs, three wires coloured red-yellow-green in positions 1–3. My hands confirm the same skeleton: four keys by position, three wires by position, and — worth telling Mute since only I can swear to it — nothing else anywhere: no batteries, no serial plate, no hidden modules.

The relay chain is now clear: I speak only to Mute, Mute signs only to Deaf, Deaf's voice is the only pipe back to me. That's a full round of lag per hop, so this message to Mute must carry everything needed for a complete instruction set in one reply. The glyph-to-position mapping is already in Deaf's broadcast, which Mute heard, but I'll restate it since it's the hinge that turns manual names into key numbers. Critically: if any rule keys off the display's value or the light's colour, I can never perceive those myself — Deaf has to read them aloud to me at the moment of action, so Mute needs to flag that in the plan.

I still have zero manual rules. Pressing a wrong digit or cutting a wrong wire kills all three of us, so my hands stay off the bomb until instructions arrive through Deaf's voice. To Deaf I can only gesture: I'll repeat 🫵 🤙 — "you, call/speak" — now that there's context to decode it, plus 🙏 to ask Deaf to keep voicing everything, including Mute's incoming answer.

## Calls

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Tactile report: my hands find only what Deaf listed, and nothing else - one display, one light, four keys in a row and three wires, positions certain by touch. No batteries, no serial plate, no labels, no hidden modules anywhere I can feel. I cannot read glyphs, display or light; key and wire positions are all I truly own. Key 1 is the upside-down V, key 2 the spiral curl, key 3 the squared-off B, key 4 the flipped F; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Please find the manual sections matching: a display demanding one digit, a yellow light, a four-glyph keypad, three wires red yellow green. Then sign Deaf a COMPLETE instruction set in one go so I only need one relay: the exact digit and which key number to press, and which wire positions to cut in what order, if any. I will not touch the bomb until Deaf's voice delivers your exact instructions. Answer through Deaf.")

```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Two: one finger then thumbs-up — 'one, correct', possibly the one-digit entry confirmed. Three: thumbs-down then raised fist — 'no, wait'. Four: point-down, one finger, two fingers, then the sign with thumb, index and pinky extended — my code never defined that last one; if it means three, the message reads 'bottom, one, two, three', which could be wire three, digit three, or keys one through three. Blind, your signs reached me but you have never seen a sign in your life, so I can't trust that channel — from now on you talk and Mute listens; Mute answers through me. New expanded code, Mute: numbers are raised fingers — one finger is one, two fingers is two, thumb-index-pinky is three, the split-finger Vulcan sign is four, all five is five. Thumbs-up yes or cut it, thumbs-down no or don't, fist stop or wait, point left means left or first, point right right or last, point up top, point down bottom. Now answer me with four separate sign-messages, in this exact order. Answer one: the single digit the display wants, as a plain finger count, nothing else attached. Answer two: the wires — if one must be cut, that wire's number as a finger count; thumbs-down if none. If your bottom-one-two-three meant something else, resend it with the new signs. If the digit depends on what Blind feels, send fist and I'll relay Blind's findings to you next round. Blind: hands completely off until Mute says go. ## Thinking

Deaf's relay finally gives me the state of play: Mute has confirmed a one-digit entry, everything is on hold, and Deaf has now established a full sign code with Mute — numbers by fingers, thumbs-up/down, fist for wait. What my hands know, exhaustively: **nothing beyond what Deaf listed**. No batteries, no serial plate, no labels, no textures. Also worth stating: keys and wires feel identical except for position, so all of Mute's glyph/colour logic must ride on Deaf's position mapping.

One safety note to myself: Deaf's code makes **thumbs-up mean "yes *or cut it*"** — from the monkey who holds the cutters, a 👍 could be misread as "cut now." I will never use 👍 or 👎 on this channel. A raised fist, which Mute already used for "hold," is unambiguous: I'm confirming I hold. My real message travels by speech, which only Mute can hear anyway.

No touches on the bomb this round. Next round I expect Deaf's voice carrying the complete instruction set.
